notes:
A tag archive is no longer told it is losing to competitors for having short pages.

Docket's thin-content check reports pages carrying too little to answer the query
they rank for. A tag or category archive is a different thing: it exists to list
what it links to, and a short one is doing its job. Docket already knew how to
tell the two apart, but only consulted that on pages under 60 words. A
publisher's tag archives — 77 to 87 words, six headlines and a line each — sit
just above that line. On one news site Docket reported 455 pages as thin content
that "lose to competitors covering the same topic properly", and every page the
report named was a tag archive. That advice was wrong for each one. The archive
test now runs across the whole thin band.

Pages that genuinely are thin articles in that band are still reported, exactly
as before. Only pages Docket's existing measured archive test already identifies
change hands.

The note Docket writes above very short archives was also overstating. It said
they "list almost nothing", which is untrue of an archive that lists six
headlines; above the very-thin band it now says they carry little beyond the
headlines they link to.

Also fixed: when exactly one retired crawler name sat above a rule that really
had stopped being enforced, the report read "1 of them sit above a Disallow …
those crawlers are reading the pages". It now reads as one.
